description: Late Iron Age farmstead, that would go onto to be abandoned in the mid 1st CE only to be re-established a little to the south in the late 1st CE. It would then go onto be re-organised multiple times and eventually show evidence of early Saxon settlement. During the Late Iron Age phase a ditched and palisaded structure would be built just to the south that has been interpreted as a shrine. It showed evidence of burning, and the deposition of a torc, vessels, and worked flint. Iron Age and Roman metalwork, including coins, were found in the vicinity.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Valley Belt, Trowse (Norfolk).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
